page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-192 is a high-capacity instance in the general-purpose family, built on the x86_64 architecture. The machine delivers 192 dedicated virtual CPUs and 744.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. This configuration provides uniform compute and memory scaling at significant single-instance density without hardware accelerators.

Hardware capabilities do not include local disk storage or discrete GPUs, requiring persistent block storage to be provisioned over the network for data persistence. Dedicated vCPU allocation ensures steady execution without CPU throttling or thread contention. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, aligning with enterprise deployments that utilize virtual private clouds and network gateways.

Consolidating 192 vCPUs onto a single node reduces inter-node networking overhead for highly distributed applications, yielding efficient utilization of large compute footprints. A key architectural tradeoff is reliance on remote persistent storage, which shifts I/O performance dependencies onto network-attached storage tiers rather than direct-attached local solid-state drives.

The c4d-standard-192 is suited for multi-threaded and high-concurrency enterprise workloads. Primary deployment targets include container orchestrators, massive CI/CD compilation clusters, batch extract-transform-load jobs, backend web serving tiers, and distributed data processing frameworks.
